name: Insect models with target selection (no priority)
bibliography: (a) Sibo Wang-Chen, Victor Alfred Stimpfling, Thomas Ka Chung Lam, Pembe Gizem Ozdil, Louise Genoud, Femke Hurtak, Pavan Ramdya. NeuroMechFly v2: simulating embodied sensorimotor control in adult Drosophila. Nature Methods 21(12), published 12 Nov 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41592-024-02497-y (venue and DOI from EPFL Infoscience/news listings; page numbers not verified); preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.09.18.556649 and EPFL postprint https://epfl.ch/labs/ramdya-lab/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NMF2_postprint.pdf - same study. Code: FlyGym (https://pypi.org/project/flygym), frozen snapshot https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12973000; data https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/3MCEYR. Uses FlyVis (Lappalainen et al., Nature 2024, https://github.com/TuragaLab/flyvis, commit 056e4aa). (b) Checked for post-2023 additions, none found that select one target among similar ones with refusal on video: searches on connectome-constrained fly pursuit/LC10, STMD/CSTMD 2024-2025 returned only pre-2023 work (Ribeiro et al. Cell 2018 LC10; Hindmarsh Sten et al. Nature 2021 LC10a/P1 network model, code https://github.com/rutalaboratory/LC10NetworkModel; Wang-Peng-Yue arXiv:1801.06687 directional STMD; CSTMD1 selective attention bioRxiv 2018) and Cowley et al. (Nature 2024, already analysed 16.10). Not repeated: CSTMD1, STMD, Wu-Guo, Cowley.
full_text_checked: NeuroMechFly v2: full text of the EPFL postprint (PDF text extracted) - Results section on fly following, Methods 'Closed-loop fly following using a connectome-constrained visual system model', Fig. 6 legend, Extended Data Fig. 7 legend, Video 14 legend, code/data availability. Figures themselves (trajectory plots) not viewed as images. Published Nature Methods version not accessible (paywall redirect); the postprint was used. Other searched works: search snippets only (no new primary source found to read).
task_and_output: NeuroMechFly v2 fly following: a simulated 'following' fly must walk after a 'leading' fly moving on a preset circular trajectory in a physics simulation; output is a descending turning drive (left/right DN drive in [0.4, 1.2]) computed from the azimuth of a detected object mask. Separate simpler task: follow a black sphere on an S-shaped path using a luminance threshold (no FlyVis).
data_and_independent_videos: No real video. Rendered visual experience of the simulated fly in MuJoCo; 11 trials per condition (flat vs 'blocks' terrain, with vs without head stabilisation, two neuron subsets) - Fig. 6h, Extended Data Fig. 7. No train/test split: FlyVis is pretrained (best single model of Lappalainen et al.) and the detector is a fixed z-score threshold.
target_size_and_input_resolution: FlyVis hexagonal ommatidia grid with side length 16 (721 columns per eye), one-to-one mapping between FlyGym and FlyVis; both eyes simulated independently. Size of the leading fly on the retina not reported [uncertain].
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Visual experience sampled at 500 Hz and FlyVis simulated at 500 Hz (modified to process one frame at a time, closed loop). Self-motion: yes - the follower walks; head stabilisation from ascending feedback is required on rugged terrain. Background: static arena; baseline activity taken from walking in an empty arena.
detector_and_exemplar: No learned detector and no exemplar: object = ommatidia where the mean z-scored deviation of selected FlyVis output activities from the empty-arena baseline exceeds chi_thr = 7 (Methods, eq. 7). Only one other object (the leading fly) is present.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: None trained in this task: pretrained FlyVis (best model of the flow ensemble) used as is; detection rule, steering and walking controller are hand-designed (the separate multimodal navigation task uses RL with a CNN, not FlyVis).
controls_seeds_splits: Conditions compared: with vs without head stabilisation; flat vs blocks terrain; readout from all T1-T5, Tm, TmY (34 putative output types) vs subset T2, T2a, T3, Tm, TmY (upstream of LC9/LC10). 11 trials each. No random/shuffled-connectome control, no non-FlyVis baseline (e.g. luminance threshold as in the sphere task) for fly following, no ensemble or seed variation (single best model).
metrics_and_numbers: Qualitative trajectory plots only: Fig. 6h and Extended Data Fig. 7 show 11 trials per case; text: following succeeds on flat terrain without head stabilisation, stabilisation 'crucial' on rugged terrain; similar results with the LC9/LC10-input subset. No numeric success rate or error stated in the text read [uncertain - plots not inspected]. Methods: chi_thr = 7, DN drive range [0.4, 1.2], turning bias update every 0.05 s, 500 Hz simulation.
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: no (simulation, no real video). Target absence: no. Similar distractors: no (single leading fly, empty arena). Occlusion: no. Night/low light: no. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes (closed loop - the follower's own steering changes its next visual input).
mechanism_summary: Published: FlyVis output-cell activities are converted into a per-column 'object score' = mean absolute z-score relative to activity statistics recorded while walking in an empty arena; columns above a threshold form the object mask; its azimuth drives steering. It is novelty/deviation detection against a learned-free baseline, not target selection. Proposed for us (not published): a per-cell-type baseline normalisation of FlyVis outputs (z-score against background-only statistics of the crop) as an input to the readout.
transfer_limits: (1) One object in an empty, static arena; no similar distractors, so no selection and no refusal - the core of Z13 is untested. (2) 500 Hz rendered input versus our 30 Hz real video with 5 fps labels; FlyVis temporal filters are tuned for high rates. (3) Baseline statistics from an empty arena are unavailable in BDD100K crops (background is cluttered and moving with the crop); a background-only baseline would have to come from the crop periphery or past frames, which already resembles our background terms in the ridge target model. (4) No real-video validation, no comparison with the eye input (luminance threshold) - the project's repeated finding that FlyVis does not beat its input is not addressed. (5) Environment YOLO/ByteTrack/MASA has no counterpart.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1: caution - the only verified FlyVis-in-closed-loop pursuit equates 'deviation from baseline above threshold' with the target; it shows nothing about choosing among similar objects or refusing. 5.2: not addressed (no target model or memory). 5.3: not addressed (no training). 5.4: not addressed. Confirms the 16.10 conclusion: no connectome/insect model selecting one of several similar targets with refusal on video has been found, also after 2023.
candidate_node_change: Not applicable as a main candidate. Minor possible readout change: z-score each FlyVis output type against background-only statistics (crop periphery, previous frames) before the target model; control without FlyVis: same z-scoring on the grey eye input; control with stock FlyVis: unnormalised outputs. Minimal check: correct re-find rate on train26 loss episodes. Stop if no gain over the eye-input control. Low priority - similar normalisation is implicit in the ridge model's background term and would not address similar neighbours.
strongest_objection: No distractors, no refusal, no real video, no baseline without FlyVis and only qualitative 11-trial plots - it demonstrates integration of FlyVis in closed loop, not a target-selection mechanism.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed (Nature Methods 2024), code and data public; FlyVis use verified in the postprint Methods (the outline's secondary claim is confirmed). Strength as evidence for Z13 mechanisms: weak (single-object, simulated, qualitative).
where_distinction_is_made: Nowhere beyond a fixed threshold: presence = any columns with z-scored deviation above chi_thr = 7; with one object, the mask maximum is the target by construction. No separation of target / similar distractor / out of area / insufficient data.
feature_dependence: Uses only FlyVis output activities (34 types, 721 columns per eye) - exactly our feature space, so no RGB dependence; but the task is trivial (one dark object on empty background) and no comparison with the raw luminance input is made, so it is no evidence that FlyVis features suffice for discrimination among similar objects.
association_consequence: Not applicable (single object, no association). An external guard is not needed in the source; for us the same effect (object vs background) is already given by the detector.
difference_from_tried: No substantive difference from what was tried: the readout is a hand-set threshold on baseline-normalised activity, weaker than the project's trained exemplar matching and online ridge target model with background terms. Only the per-type z-score against background statistics is not explicitly tried as a separate normalisation [uncertain - may be equivalent to existing feature standardisation in the ridge model].
refusal_evidence_horizon: Not applicable (no refusal); detection is single-frame thresholding, steering updated every 0.05 s.
no_fly_control_equivalent: Luminance threshold on the rendered retina (exactly what the same paper uses for the black-sphere task) - a direct no-fly control that the authors did not report for fly following.
hard_subset_evaluation: No; only terrain difficulty (flat vs blocks) as a harder condition.
temporal_information_availability: Causal, online: current and past frames only (FlyVis run frame by frame at 500 Hz; steering updated every 0.05 s). No future frames.
depth_level: Short screening. Lost: single target without distractors or refusal in simulation, no real video, no non-FlyVis baseline. No new post-2023 insect/connectome target-selection model was found; the item should not move to full analysis. Value: confirms the secondary claim and records that the only closed-loop FlyVis pursuit uses a baseline z-score threshold.
